pr_title: Fix entering a playlist room potentially showing settings screen incorrectly
pr_body:
Would happen when the ruleset did not match.

Closes #14091.

issue_context.title: Joining a playlist potentially shows settings screen instead of room
issue_context.body:
This looks like it happens for a playlist with difficulties from different rulesets, where the current game's ruleset doesn't match the first playlist item.


When it does match, the room opens correctly:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/127768011-46ae3d87-cfba-4121-be62-afe3b9f78082.mp4

When it doesn't match, the settings are shown and it's not possible to get into the actual room:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/127768038-40f6e8f3-22ff-40cc-8671-596a167d0de3.mp4
comments:
On a quick check the sequence of events here is as follows:

* The playlist is joined, switching ruleset from (current user ruleset) to (ruleset of the first playlist item)
* This changes filter criteria in the (still-visible) playlists screen
* Therefore a re-poll of the playlist rooms is triggered
* This re-poll clears all rooms in the room manager
* If all of this occurs *after* the actual room is joined and set, the settings overlay will display (ie. this is a race - if the actual room set loses the race and executes after all of that, everything will work "as expected").

Feels like the lounge screen should take exclusive control over the current room, I think?

review_comments:
There are more writes to `selectedRoom` in this class than this one, and they can crash because they're bound to UI items. `OnClick()` may be mostly safe thanks to the loading layer in front, but `selectNext()` can most definitely blow up.

This would be best reproducible by attaching a delay between `LoungeSubScreen` taking the lease and the room subscreen being pushed, and then spamming arrow up/down during that delay. I used the debugger to help me with that, but it sure does crash.

Maybe we can remove the global selected room bindable... After the lounge redesign, it'll only be used for the multiplayer background but perhaps it's possible to simplify that flow without using a bindable.
Do you think it's worth doing that refactor here? At very least, it would require moving the scroll container inside `RoomsContainer` as it is currently being used there.
It may be slightly too complex to refactor as part of this PR.
To avoid growing this PR any further (and just fix the underlying issue, which is a pretty serious one) I've stuck to fixing the remaining two operations in a hope to get it in a release today.
